title: Starter Resources — Watch These First
tag: Three 1-hour talks from Andrej Karpathy covering foundations, deep dive, and practical use.
learn: Get a complete mental model from the expert (Karpathy, ex-Tesla AI director). Three complementary perspectives: foundation, technical depth, and hands-on practice.
do: Watch in order: Intro → Deep Dive → Practical. Take notes. These replace a textbook.
objectives: Understand LLM architecture, training, and inference from first principles
See real-world examples of how LLMs succeed and fail
Learn practical patterns for using LLMs in your own work
checkpoint: Take 3 key insights from the three videos and write them down. No essay needed—bullets are fine.

resources.title: Andrej Karpathy — Intro to Large Language Models
Andrej Karpathy — Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT (Latest)
Andrej Karpathy — How I use LLMs (Practical)

watchouts: Watch all three in order. Karpathy's latest video (Deep Dive) covers recent developments. Don't skip—these are the foundation for everything else.
tools: Maybe Claude or ChatGPT to test concepts

title: How LLMs Actually Work
tag: Build the mental model that explains both the power and the failures.
learn: Understand transformers, tokens, attention, and why LLMs hallucinate.
do: Read Karpathy's blog and watch 3Blue1Brown; play with the tokenizer; write your first prompt.
objectives: Build a correct mental model of transformers: what is attention, embeddings, and why it works?
Predict where LLMs will help versus where they'll confidently mislead you.
Understand the token economy: how tokens relate to cost and context window limits.
checkpoint: Write a 2-paragraph explanation of how attention works. Mention: embeddings, attention mechanism, why it matters.

resources.title: Andrej Karpathy — A Recipe for Training Neural Networks (blog)
Hugging Face — What is a Transformer?

watchouts: This feels theoretical, but it's the foundation. Understanding attention explains why verification matters (Week 4).

title: Capabilities, Limits & Failure Modes
tag: Know what can go wrong and when hallucinations actually matter.
learn: Understand hallucinations, scaling laws, in-context learning, and when to trust LLM output.
do: Read real incident cases; test a hallucination yourself; build a skepticism checklist.
objectives: Recognize hallucinations and understand why they happen (probability, not retrieval).
Know when hallucinations are acceptable vs. when they're a blocker.
Understand in-context learning and why 5-shot prompting beats 1-shot.
checkpoint: List 3 infrastructure scenarios where hallucinations are OK. List 3 where they're NOT OK. Explain the difference.

resources.title: Mollick — How to Use AI to Do Stuff
Logan Kilpatrick — Why Do LLMs Hallucinate?

watchouts: Bigger models hallucinate less, but they still hallucinate. Confidence is not truth.

title: Practical Integration — Prompting & APIs
tag: Write effective prompts and understand how to integrate LLMs into your workflows.
learn: Master prompting structure, cost modeling, RAG patterns, and tool calling.
do: Write 3 real prompts for your infrastructure work; explore LangChain; estimate costs.
objectives: Write effective technical prompts (with context, constraints, examples).
Understand LLM API economics: tokens, batch processing, caching, cost optimization.
Know when to use RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) and how to build it.
checkpoint: Test 3 prompts in Claude or ChatGPT for your actual infrastructure work. Report: did they work? How would you improve?
watchouts: Good prompts have structure. Vague prompts = vague outputs. Test and iterate.

title: Safety, Governance & Capstone
tag: Learn to use LLMs responsibly in production and document your first workflow.
learn: Build verification checklists, protect secrets, evaluate quality, and design safe workflows.
do: Redact a real log; build a verification checklist; submit capstone project.
objectives: Design verification and fallback mechanisms for LLM-assisted infrastructure tasks.
Keep secrets, PII, and proprietary code out of prompts.
Understand your org's AI policy and shadow-AI exposure.
checkpoint: Submit a capstone: document one LLM-assisted workflow you'd deploy. Include: the workflow, where LLM helps, your prompt, verification step, one risk, cost estimate.

resources.title: OpenAI — Our Approach to AI Safety

watchouts: This module is the guardrail. Unverified output and leaked secrets are how adoption fails. Treat verification as core engineering.
